justification: Changes the flood classification text shown on the property page: every flood level the lot is mapped in, most frequent first, instead of the first value in text order.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: 0.2% AEP is listed before 1% AEP, or a level the map gives is dropped
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 2026-10-29: route.ts used dcpFloodRows[0].value; the SQL sorts values as text, so '0.2%AEP' sorted before '1%AEP' (spatial_overlays flood values: 1%AEP, PMF, 20.0%AEP, 0.2%AEP, 0.5%AEP, 1.0%AEP, 5.0%AEP, 2.0%AEP).

pre_impl.existing_data: spatial_overlays layer flood holds AEP and PMF values; a lot can intersect several.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The route assumed rows[0] was the meaningful value; it is only the first by text.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One helper used at the one place the classification is set; same field and type.

functions.name: floodLevels
functions.input: the flood overlay values for the address point and its lot
functions.output: distinct levels joined, AEP by frequency descending, then PMF, then others
functions.if_none: no values gives undefined and the badge shows Yes as before

values.if_missing: an empty or null value is skipped

break_it.scenario: A lot is in both the 1% and 0.2% AEP areas.
break_it.what_happens: The badge must not show only the milder level.
break_it.how: Both are listed, 1% AEP first; test added.

break_it.scenario: A council stores the same level two ways (1%AEP, 1.0%AEP).
break_it.what_happens: The badge would list one level twice.
break_it.how: Numeric key folds them; test added.

break_it.scenario: A flood value that is not an AEP or PMF.
break_it.what_happens: It could be dropped or misordered.
break_it.how: Kept, after the known levels; test added.
